subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
title: Jesus raises a Widow’s Son
overview: Luke 7:11-16 tells how Jesus met a funeral at the town of Nain and raised a widow's only son. In this sub-strand you will retell that miracle, recognise God's power over life and death, and learn to show compassion and to pray when life is hard. You will also recite John 11:25.

lessons.title: The funeral at Nain
objectives: Explain how the story shows God's power over life and death.
lessons.intro: A funeral is a day of tears. At Nain, a widow was burying her only son. Jesus met that procession at the town gate and showed that death does not have the last word.
lessons.notes:
Read Luke 7:11-16 and retell it carefully.

Soon afterwards, Jesus went to a town called Nain. His disciples and a large crowd went with Him. As He approached the town gate, a dead person was being carried out. The dead man was the only son of his mother, and she was a widow. A large crowd from the town was with her.

When the Lord saw her, His heart went out to her and He said, "Don't cry." He went up and touched the bier they were carrying the body on, and the bearers stood still. He said, "Young man, I say to you, get up!" The dead man sat up and began to talk, and Jesus gave him back to his mother.

The people were filled with awe and praised God. They said, "A great prophet has appeared among us," and "God has come to help His people."

### Power over life and death
The young man was dead. Jesus spoke, and he sat up and talked. People do not raise the dead. God does. The crowd was right to praise God. They saw that God had come to help His people.

John 11:25 is a word of Jesus to learn beside this story: "I am the resurrection and the life. The one who believes in me will live, even though they die." Resurrection means being raised to life. Write the verse on a flash card and recite it.

This miracle does not mean we should expect every funeral to end as Nain's did. It means Jesus has real power over death, and those who believe in Him have His promise of life. We still comfort people who are bereaved. We do not pretend that death is small. We trust the Lord who told the young man to get up.

keyWords.meaning: a woman whose husband has died
the frame on which the body was carried

activity.title: Read the story and the verse
steps: Read Luke 7:11-16 and retell the story.
If a video clip on the raising of the widow's son is available, watch it and compare it with the verses.
Write John 11:25 on a flash card and recite it.
Say how the story shows God's power over life and death.
Sing a song about God's power over life and death.

practice.question: Who had died, and what was his mother's situation?
practice.answer: The only son of a widow had died. The funeral was leaving the town of Nain.

practice.question: What did Jesus say to the young man, and what happened?
practice.answer: He said, "Young man, I say to you, get up!" The dead man sat up, began to talk, and Jesus gave him back to his mother.

practice.question: Recite John 11:25.
practice.answer: I am the resurrection and the life. The one who believes in me will live, even though they die.

summary: At Nain, Jesus met the funeral of a widow's only son.
He told the young man to get up, and the man sat up and spoke.
John 11:25: Jesus is the resurrection and the life.

lessons.title: Compassion and prayer in hard times
objectives: Say how Jesus showed compassion to the widow.
Show compassion to others and pray when facing challenges.
lessons.intro: Jesus did not pass the widow in silence. His heart went out to her. Compassion is that movement of the heart, followed by help. We can learn it, and we can pray when our own troubles come.
lessons.notes:
Compassion means feeling someone's pain and acting to help. Luke 7:13 says that when the Lord saw the widow, His heart went out to her. He told her not to cry. Then He did more than speak. He touched the bier, raised her son, and gave him back to her. Compassion in this story is pity joined to power.

### Lessons for us
We do not have power to raise the dead. We do have ways to show kindness:

- Sit with someone who is sad and listen.
- Say a gentle word instead of laughing at tears.
- Help with a small task at a neighbour's home when a family is in trouble.
- Share food or a school item with a child who has lost support.
- Pray for the person.
- Tell a parent or teacher if a classmate is deeply sad or unsafe.

Social justice in a child's life includes this kindness. You do not ignore a person in pain.

### Praying when you face challenges
Challenges are hard things: sickness, lack of school needs, fear, a quarrel, or grief. List yours honestly. Then say how you involve God:

- Tell Him the problem in prayer.
- Ask for help, wisdom and comfort.
- Thank Him for the people who stand with you.
- Obey what is right while you wait.
- Remember John 11:25 when you are afraid of death: Jesus is the resurrection and the life.

The widow did not have to shout for Jesus to care. He saw her. You may still pray, because prayer is how you bring your challenge to the God who sees. Depend on Him for the solution, and accept the help of trusted adults.

keyWords.meaning: feeling someone's pain and acting to help
the deep sadness that comes when someone dies or a great loss happens

activity.title: Kindness and prayer
steps: Say how Jesus showed compassion to the widow.
Tell how you show kindness to others.
List challenges you face and how you involve God.
Write a short prayer asking God for help with one challenge.
Recite John 11:25 and sing about God's power.

practice.question: How did Jesus show compassion to the widow?
practice.answer: His heart went out to her, He told her not to cry, He raised her son, and He gave him back to her.

practice.question: Give two ways a learner can show compassion.
practice.answer: Any two: listen to someone who is sad, speak gently, help with a task, share food or a school item, pray, tell an adult if someone is unsafe.

practice.question: What should you do when you face a challenge?
practice.answer: Pray and tell God the problem, ask for help, and also seek help from trusted adults.

summary: Jesus' heart went out to the widow, and He gave her son back.
We show compassion by kind words and helpful actions.
We pray to God when we face challenges.

quiz.question: The raising of the widow's son is told in:
The town was...
quiz.explanation: Luke 7:11 says Jesus went to a town called Nain.

quiz.question: The dead person was...
quiz.explanation: Luke 7:12 says he was the only son of his mother, and she was a widow.

quiz.question: What happened when Jesus said, "Young man, get up"?
quiz.answer: The dead man sat up and began to talk, and Jesus gave him back to his mother.

quiz.question: The crowd praised God and said...
options: God has come to help His people

quiz.question: John 11:25 says Jesus is...
quiz.explanation: The verse says, "I am the resurrection and the life."

quiz.question: God's power over death in this story is seen when:
quiz.answer: Jesus raised the widow's son and the young man sat up and spoke.
quiz.explanation: Only God's power can raise the dead.

quiz.question: Jesus showed compassion when...
options: His heart went out to the widow and He helped her
He told the crowd to be silent forever
quiz.explanation: Luke 7:13 says His heart went out to her.

quiz.question: When you face a challenge you should...
options: pray and ask God for help
quiz.explanation: The lesson teaches learners to pray when they face challenges.
